payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

outcomes.description: Add a helmet to the woman.
outcomes.target: The woman is wearing or otherwise visibly has a helmet on her head.
outcomes.reference: The woman in the input image.

nodes.question: Does the image show a helmet visibly on the woman’s head?
nodes.criteria: Pass if a helmet is visibly on the woman’s head; fail if the image clearly shows no helmet on her head; unknown if the woman or her head is not visible enough to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess only the woman in the input image and whether she is wearing or otherwise visibly has a helmet on her head. Ignore unrelated edits.

nodes.question: Is there image evidence that a helmet has been added to the woman, even if the requested result is not complete?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows a helmet on or being placed on the woman’s head, but the evidence does not establish the complete result in s1; fail if the image clearly shows no progress toward adding a helmet; unknown if visibility is insufficient to determine whether such progress occurred. A complete result is not partial progress.
nodes.binding: Assess only visible evidence of progress toward giving the woman in the input image a helmet. Do not count unrelated changes as progress.

nodes.question: Is a helmet visibly present on the woman’s head?
nodes.criteria: For R1, complete if s1 passes. Partial if s1 does not pass and s2 passes. Absent if s1 and s2 both fail. Unknown if neither complete nor partial nor absent is established because a required check is unknown. Unrelated edits do not count as progress; unknown evidence remains unresolved.
nodes.binding: Target: The woman is wearing or otherwise visibly has a helmet on her head.. Reference: The woman in the input image..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The fulfillment readout cannot faithfully distinguish a complete result from partial progress. s2 is defined to pass only when it shows progress but does not establish the complete result in s1, yet the readout says partial if s1 does not pass and s2 passes. If s1 is unknown while s2 passes, this can label the result partial without establishing incompleteness; if s1 fails, the checks may also conflict about whether a helmet is present. The composition should require evidenced incompleteness before assigning partial and resolve contradictory support observations rather than treating them as a valid outcome."}
